parts.text:
Both parallel test jobs finished fast: `auto/hy3` → 60/60 done, 0 errors, 83.3% accuracy; `workbuddy/deepseek-v4.1-flash` → 60/60 done, 0 errors. They ran **in parallel at full speed**, which tells me magpie's limit is roughly *per-route* (each route gets its own ~1–2 slots), not a single global cap — so running models across different routes in parallel multiplies throughput. The earlier slow `auto/hy4free` was just the reasoning model itself being slow + flooded at concurrency 8 (timeouts).

Fix: lower per-model concurrency to 3 (avoids timeout floods) and orchestrate across routes in parallel. Let me confirm PowerShell 7 (for `ForEach-Object -Parallel`) and set concurrency.

The cleanest approach is a single Python orchestrator that runs each route-prefix as its own sequential group, with up to 6 groups in parallel (different routes → independent magpie capacity), and auto-generates the combined report at the end. Let me write it.

tool_input.content:
import subprocess, sys, os, time
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor

WORK = r"C:\Users\Administrator\Documents\deepseek-harness\default-workspace\mmvp-bench"
os.chdir(WORK)
DATA = "mmvp_eval.jsonl"
REG = "models.yaml"

# One group per distinct magpie route prefix -> runs sequentially within a group,
# but up to 6 groups run in parallel (different routes get independent magpie capacity).
groups = {
    'auto':         ['auto/hy4free', 'auto/hy3', 'auto/deepseek-v4.1-flash'],
    'cursor':       ['cursor/grok-4.7@256k', 'cursor/composer-2.5', 'cursor/deepseek-v41-flash-1017'],
    'workbuddy':    ['workbuddy/hy4free', 'workbuddy/hy3', 'workbuddy/deepseek-v4.1-flash'],
    'workbuddy-ai': ['workbuddy-ai/hy4free', 'workbuddy-ai/hy3'],
    'minimax-code': ['minimax-code/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash'],
    'autoclaw-cn':  ['autoclaw-cn/zai_glm-5.3-flash'],
}

def run_group(name, models):
    with open(f"orch_{name}.log", "a", encoding="utf-8") as log:
        for m in models:
            log.write(f"===== START {m} {time.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')} =====\n"); log.flush()
            t0 = time.time()
            p = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "vlmeter", "run",
                                "--models", m, "--data", DATA, "--registry", REG],
                               cwd=WORK, stdout=log, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
            log.write(f"===== END {m} exit={p.returncode} {time.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')} "
                      f"({time.time()-t0:.0f}s) =====\n"); log.flush()

try:
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=6) as ex:
        list(ex.map(lambda kv: run_group(kv[0], kv[1]), groups.items()))
    print("ALL GROUPS DONE")
except Exception as e:
    print("ORCH ERROR:", repr(e))

r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "vlmeter", "report", "--data", DATA], cwd=WORK)
print("REPORT exit", r.returncode)
print("ALL_DONE")

import subprocess, sys, os, time

WORK = r"C:\Users\Administrator\Documents\deepseek-harness\default-workspace\mmvp-bench"

DATA = "mmvp_eval.jsonl"
REG = "models.yaml"

for m in models:
    ts = time.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')

    p = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "vlmeter", "run",

print("REPORT exit", r.returncode)
print("WORKBUDDY_DONE")
